label: Confirmed Cases (2026 DRC + Uganda + France)
source: DRC Ministry of Health / ECDC / CIDRAP — 19–20 August 2026
contestNote: DRC: 5,208 confirmed cases and 2,476 deaths as of 18 August, published 19 August. Uganda's outbreak was declared officially over 28 July 2026 (20 confirmed, 18 recoveries, 2 deaths). France: 1 case, recovered and discharged 4 July, no secondary transmission. WHO estimates true DRC case count could be up to 4x higher than reported given ongoing active transmission and community mistrust limiting detection.
deltaNote: DRC confirmed cases roughly thirteenfold since early June: 400 (June 5) → 2,011 (July 15) → 3,605 (July 30) → 4,053 (August 5) → 4,665 (August 13) → 4,945 (August 16) → 5,021 (August 18) → 5,208 (August 19). This is now the largest Ebola outbreak in DRC history and the second-largest ever recorded worldwide, behind only the 2014-16 West Africa epidemic (28,616 cases). Case count formally passed 5,000 on 19 August — the fastest any Ebola outbreak has reached that scale.

source: DRC Ministry of Health / ECDC / CIDRAP — 19–20 August 2026
deltaNote: The 19 August DRC situation report (data through 18 August) recorded an increase of 187 confirmed cases and 98 deaths from the prior day's report alone. 730 patients currently hospitalized in isolation in DRC. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus told the second IHR Emergency Committee on 18 August 'we must be frank: the epidemic is far from being under control,' adding it 'is moving faster than any previous Ebola outbreak.'

label: Deaths (2026 Outbreak)
source: DRC Ministry of Health / ECDC / CIDRAP — 19–20 August 2026
contestNote: Confirmed deaths: 2,476 DRC + 2 Uganda = 2,478 total as of 18 August, published 19 August. CFR (confirmed): ~47.5% (2,476/5,208 DRC), reaching roughly 70% in North Kivu province specifically. The toll surpassed the 2,299 deaths of DRC's 2018-2020 Kivu outbreak, making this the deadliest Ebola outbreak in the country's history — deaths rose from 1,000 to 2,000 in under a month, the fastest fatal surge in Ebola's recorded history. UN humanitarian chief Tom Fletcher said the outbreak was killing one person every 30 minutes as of 14 August. WHO reports most deaths continue to occur in communities away from treatment centers.
deltaNote: DRC confirmed deaths: 64 (June 5) → 754 (July 15) → 1,587 (July 30) → 1,850 (August 5) → 2,184 (August 13) → 2,325 (August 16) → 2,378 (August 18) → 2,476 (August 19). 155 confirmed cases among healthcare workers, 45 deaths (29% CFR among HCWs).

label: Case Fatality Rate (2026 BDBV)
value: ~47.5% (DRC, crude, as of 18 Aug); ~70% in North Kivu
source: DRC Ministry of Health / ECDC / CIDRAP / Africanews — 19–20 August 2026
contestNote: Crude national CFR calculated from reported confirmed cases/deaths; DRC's overall CFR has climbed from roughly 20% in early June to ~47.5% by 18-19 August as the outbreak has spread into less-accessible, less-resourced health zones. Province-level variation is stark: North Kivu's CFR has reached roughly 70%, well above the national average, which responders and outside experts attribute to weaker treatment access rather than a change in virus behavior. BDBV historically 25–47% CFR; this outbreak's crude national CFR now sits at or above the top of the historical range.

label: BDBV Vaccine Status — 70,000 Ervebo Doses Allocated, Phase 3 Trial Imminent
value: 70,000 Ervebo doses released to DRC (20,000 for Phase 3 trial + 50,000 for frontline/health workers); trial not yet launched
source: WHO / Africa CDC / International Coordinating Group on Vaccine Provision — 20 August 2026
contestNote: 20 August: WHO and Africa CDC announced the ICG approved immediate release of 70,000 Ervebo (rVSV-ZEBOV) doses to DRC — 20,000 for a Phase 3 clinical trial testing cross-protection against Bundibugyo virus, 50,000 for frontline and health workers. WHO cautioned 'it is not known whether Ervebo may be protective against the Bundibugyo virus in humans,' though early lab/animal data suggest possible partial protection. As of 20 August the trial itself had not yet launched — shipment, DRC regulatory/ethics approval and team training remain outstanding. Animal data: 3/4 vaccinated primates survived BDBV challenge vs 1/4 controls; a ferret study showed 100% protection with a research-grade formulation vs 0% in controls. Oxford's ChAdOx1 BDBV and IAVI's rVSV BDBV remain in earlier-stage human trials and may be added later.
delta: 70,000-dose allocation approved 20 August, up from advancing talks as of 12 August
deltaNote: The 28 May WHO expert panel ruling barred Ervebo use outside research settings; the 7 August TAG-CVP recommendation, 12 August trial talks, and 20 August dose allocation are successive steps toward a structured clinical trial pathway rather than a resumption of off-label ring vaccination. Since the ICG mechanism's 2021 establishment, over 56,000 Ervebo doses have been allocated for DRC outbreaks combined, plus 167,000 doses in preventive campaigns across five countries.

source: DRC Ministry of Health / ECDC / Africa CDC — 19–20 August 2026

deltaNote: Ituri Province remains the epicenter with the large majority of DRC cases; North Kivu, Haut-Uélé, Tshopo, South Kivu and Bas-Uélé round out the six affected provinces. Bas-Uélé borders Central African Republic conflict-displacement corridors and has poor road/communications access. Uganda's outbreak (Kampala + Wakiso) was declared over 28 July. Mambasa Territory (IS-controlled) remains largely inaccessible to response teams. The second WHO IHR Emergency Committee meeting on PHEIC status was held 18 August; Tedros said the epidemic 'is far from being under control.'

label: Contact Tracing Coverage (DRC)
value: ~85.3% of identified contacts under active follow-up
delta: Coverage improved from ~82.7% (12 August) and ~45% (June) but 60-70% of new cases are still occurring outside monitored contacts
deltaNote: ECDC reported active follow-up at 85.3% of identified contacts as of the 16 August update, up from 82.7% on 10 August — still below the 90%+ threshold needed for rapid suppression. Mercy Corps separately warned 60-70% of new cases are recorded outside monitored contacts, with confirmed cases now just 35km from the South Sudan border. Uganda's contact-tracing program is closed following the 28 July outbreak-end declaration. Mambasa Territory (IS-controlled) remains a contact-tracing dead zone.
